agent_vs_you: The agent's chain is the right one (image, then image-to-video of that image, both kept) and the animation prompt is good: the cat blinks and swishes its tail, silent, square. The defect was born in the still: flux-2-klein drew the cat with two striped tails, and the 120-credit animation faithfully carried both. The agent's still prompt pushed 'with its tail clearly visible' without saying one tail or where it lies, and it animated without checking the 5-credit still first. I would name a single tail and its position, and gate the animation on a check of the still. The 'no standalone picture' finding is the grader's: the still exists, but deliverables() only counts sink nodes (plus a few code tools), so an intermediate the user asked for is invisible to it.

your_plan.say: I'll paint the square illustration first, check it, then animate that same picture for 5 seconds with a slow blink and a gentle tail swish, silent. You'll get both the picture and the video.

params.prompt_or_change: Warm storybook-style digital illustration, soft golden light: a fluffy orange tabby cat with exactly one tail, wearing a blue knitted scarf, sitting upright on a sunny wooden windowsill and facing the viewer, its single striped tail curled along the sill to the left of its front paws; a potted plant beside it and sunlight streaming through the window. Natural cat anatomy: four legs, one tail. No text.

steps.why: Deliverable 1, and the animation's first frame; one tail and its place are stated so the model does not draw a second.

params.prompt_or_change: Does the cat have exactly one tail and four legs, an orange coat and a blue scarf, sitting on a sunny windowsill, with no text?

steps.why: A 0-credit gate before 120 credits of animation; anatomy is where klein slips.

params.prompt_or_change: Subtle animation of this illustration with a locked-off camera: the cat blinks slowly twice and its one tail sways gently back and forth along the sill; the scarf, the window light and the room stay exactly as they are, illustration style unchanged.

steps.why: Deliverable 2: the same picture moving; its invented sound is dropped by default, so it is silent.

fix: 1) Planner rule: when a generated still feeds an expensive animation, add a check of the still (anatomy, counts, text) before the clip, and state counts of body parts that will move (one tail). 2) Let a failed check trigger one regeneration of the still before the video step runs. 3) Plan schema and grader: let a step be marked deliver: true (the agent already said 'I'll deliver both'), and have deliverables() count marked intermediates, not only sinks; today a requested picture that feeds a video is never counted, so every 'picture and its animation' item fails 'too-few-outputs'.
evidence: cat_illustration.png (klein, 640x640) shows an orange tabby in a blue scarf on a sunny windowsill, with TWO striped tails: one curling forward on the sill left of the paws, a second hanging off the sill on the right. cat_animation.mp4 (480x480, 5.17 s, video stream only, so silent) carries both tails in every sampled frame (0, 1.25, 2.5, 3.75, 5 s); the cat's eyes are closed at ~1.25 s (blink) and the left tail swings, so the motion itself met the brief. The grader saw only the mp4 because the still is consumed by image-to-video and is not a sink.
